paper_title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Large language models can reason in continuous space instead of decoded text, by recurring on their own hidden states or by passing those states between agents, while training supervises only the Cross-Entropy (CE) of the final decoded answer and does not constrain the thought. Theoretical and empirical analyses establish and confirm four failures of CE-only training that lead to a lower probability of the correct answer such as collapsing thoughts across distinct questions and retaining irrelevant information. We introduce REST (REpresentation-Supervised Thoughts), a training objective that turns four properties of a valid thought representation (causality, minimality, separability, and stability) into differentiable losses added to CE. We instantiate it in latent single-agent and multi-agent systems, without architectural changes or added parameters at inference. Across 7 benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, medicine, and code generation, with the same training data, compute, and latent budget, REST increases accuracy over CE-only training across agent settings and model sizes by up to 7.5 percentage points and convergence on a final answer by 30\%. Furthermore, REST thoughts encode more of what is required to achieve the correct answer, and decoding them better recovers the intended output of the agent, which makes latent communication easier to interpret. Project Website: https://fard-lab.github.io/REST

sections.title: 1 INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to solve complex problems by generating each intermediate reasoning step as explicit text (Wei et al., 2022). However, expressing every step through tokens of discrete vocabulary confines reasoning to paths that can be written in words (Li et al., 2025). The resulting reasoning traces are also long, which raises inference cost and leads models to allocate excessive computation to simple problems (Chen et al., 2025a). To resolve these limitations, growing line of work reasons directly in the continuous latent space of LLMs rather than through decoded text (Hao et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2025; Butt et al., 2026; Shen et al., 2025; Wei et al., 2026; Sheshanarayana et al., 2026). Within single model, this is realized by training the model to consume its own hidden states as the next reasoning step instead of token embedding (Hao et al., 2026; Shen et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026a). From one model to another, hidden states or KV caches have instead been used for inter-agent communication (Liu et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2026). Recent systems unify both, with multiple agents reasoning and communicating in latent space (Zou et al., 2026b) and repeating this collaboration over several rounds of recursion (Zou et al., 2026a). The main objective is usually Cross-Entropy (CE) of the final decoded answer. As these systems scale in agents and rounds, each later agent builds on the thoughts it receives, and error compounds through the remainder of the system. Existing representation-level supervision targets the text the thought replaces, which CODI does by matching the hidden states that text induces (Shen et al., 2025) or SIM-COT by decoding that text back from the thought (Wei et al., 2026). However, supervising only on the target text does not dictate the relation between two thoughts nor the distribution of outputs the model can generate. Both requirements are among the four properties that define valid thought representation (Seddik & Fard, 2026). valid thought representation should preserve what is needed to reproduce the output (Causality), discard what is irrelevant to that output (Minimality), remain distinguishable across semantically distinct inputs (Separability), and reflect the distribution of possible outputs rather than one sample from it (Stability). An audit of existing latent representations finds that every candidate violates at least one property. The audit evaluates existing methods, and does not perform training to target these properties. Training with CE only does not enforce them either, since model receives no signal as long as the correct answer maintains high probability (Section 2.1). Figure 2: Overview of REST. Latent systems pass thought through trained outer link (left). REST adds β-weighted loss built from the four properties of to the CE objective (middle). CE-only thoughts collapse and REST improves accuracy under the same data and compute (right). We introduce REpresentation-Supervised Thought(s) (REST). REST translates each of these four properties into differentiable loss term (Section A.1) and adds it to the total loss alongside CE. Each term is weighted by hyperparameter β, added on top of the existing CE loss. Training then targets the thought representation as well as the decoded answer (Figure 2). REST is studied on latent recursive system in which the base LLMs are frozen (Zou et al., 2026a). We extend this construction from the multi-agent setting in which it was proposed to single-agent setting, where model recurs on its own hidden states. In addition, no changes to architecture or inference procedure are required, allowing it to be added to existing latent recursive systems without modification. REST increases downstream accuracy across MATH500 (Lightman et al., 2024), GPQA-Diamond (Rein et al., 2024), MedQA (Jin et al., 2021), AIME2025/2026 (Zhang & Math-AI Team, 2025; Dekoninck et al., 2026), LiveCodeBench-v6 (Jain et al., 2025), and MBPP+ (Liu et al., 2023), spanning mathematical, scientific, and code-generation domains. Averaged over all REST configurations, it improves accuracy over CE only by +3. 2 Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems points in the multi-agent setting and +3.3 in the single-agent setting, under matched training budget, the same training data, and the same latent budget. The best configurations reach +7.5 and +6.5 points, respectively. Through our analysis, we confirm that the trained thoughts exhibit the properties that were targeted, which in turn lower-bound the probability of the correct answer (Section A.2). REST decodes 15.4% more tokens on average at inference, which we attribute to higher rate of convergence on final answer (Section 4.4). Our contributions can be summarized as follows: We identify four failures of CE-only thoughts that lead to lower probability of the correct answer (Section 2.1). In trained systems, CE-only thoughts collapse across distinct questions and retain irrelevant information (Section 4.4). We introduce REST, which translates four theoretically motivated properties of thought representations (Seddik & Fard, 2026) into differentiable loss terms added to the CE objective, and we extend latent recursive systems (Zou et al., 2026a) from the multi-agent setting to single agent that recurs on its own hidden states. REST improves accuracy over the CE baseline across mathematical, scientific, medical, and codegeneration benchmarks in both the single-agent and multi-agent settings, under matched training and latent budgets, and its gains remain robust across loss weights.

sections.title: 3.3 SINGLE-AGENT SYSTEMS
sections.content: It is important to note that Definition 2.1 permits Ai = Aj, which corresponds to our extension to the single-agent setting. REST extends to single agent reasoning in latent space, rather than being restricted to pipeline of several agents. Self-Loop. single solver acts as both the producer and the consumer, with no planner and no refiner (Figure 4). The solver first runs on its own input context and computes last-layer hidden states. These states pass through the frozen inner link Rin and the trained outer link Rψ, which gives the thought of Section 2. The solver then runs second time, conditioned on both its own input context and T. Each further round repeats the second pass, and the hidden states it computes form the next rounds thought. Equation (7) applies at = 1. The two links act at different points of the system. Rin runs at every one of the latent steps and lets the solver take latent step instead of decoding token, whereas Rψ runs once per round. Removing Rin therefore removes latent reasoning itself rather than one trainable component. Keeping it frozen leaves ψ as the only parameter that varies between CE and REST, and between the singleand multi-agent settings. Figure 4: Single agent. Rin runs at each of the steps, and Rψ once per round.

sections.title: 5 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Reasoning in Latent Space. Recent work treats the continuous latent space of an LLM as the medium of reasoning rather than the decoded text (Chen et al., 2026b; Zhu et al., 2025). Within single model, hidden states re-enter the input stream as the next reasoning step (Zhang et al., 2025; Tan et al., 2025; Butt et al., 2026; Sheshanarayana et al., 2026; Li et al., 2026a). Across models, hidden representations and KV caches carry information between agents in place of text (Liu et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2025; Zheng et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2026; Ye et al., 2025; Zou et al., 2026b). further line reuses the same computation over several rounds to deepen latent reasoning (Geiping et al., 2025; Zhu et al., 2026; Jolicoeur-Martineau, 2025; Bae et al., 2025), which Zou et al. (2026a) raise to the system level by looping heterogeneous agents through learned link. Most of these systems rely on the cross-entropy of the final decoded answer for training, and typically leave the latent thoughts themselves unconstrained. Figure 8: Positioning of REST. Supervising Latent Thoughts. The signal that trains latent state is the answer following the latent steps (Hao et al., 2026), self-distilled explicit chain of thought (Shen et al., 2025), or an auxiliary decoder aligning every latent step with its explicit counterpart (Wei et al., 2026). Each of these signals is defined against reference the latent state must reproduce, either text or another models own cache (Chen et al., 2026a). Audits of the resulting representations report high accuracy without latent reasoning, collapsed candidate solutions, and unstable trajectories (Cui et al., 2026; Rizvi-Martel et al., 2026; Sahoo et al., 2026). recent 9 Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems framework states four properties valid thought representation should satisfy, and audits existing methods against them (Seddik & Fard, 2026). REST is the first to turn the theoretically motivated properties of valid thought representation into loss terms for latent recursive LLM system (Figure 8). Additional related work in Section C.

sections.title: 6 CONCLUSION
sections.content: We introduce REST, training objective that supervises the thoughts of latent recursive LLM systems through four properties of valid thought representation. Our objective translates causality, minimality, separability, and stability into differentiable loss terms added to CE. These terms require no architectural changes or added parameters at inference. Theoretical analyses show that the failures these properties prevent lead to lower probability of the correct answer. Empirically, thoughts trained only with CE collapse across distinct questions and retain irrelevant information. Evaluations across mathematical, scientific, medical, and code-generation benchmarks demonstrate that REST improves accuracy over CE in both singleand multi-agent settings. Overall, REST establishes principled way to supervise latent thoughts beyond the final decoded answer. Implications. The improvements from an auxiliary term in both settings indicate that CE-only insufficiently constrains latent thoughts, and that latent recursive systems benefit from supervising the thought representation. The property that yields the largest gain further depends on the consumer, as causality leads when the thought passes to different agent and minimality leads when model recurs on its own thought. Since the collapse and input content observed under CE are not reflected in the CE objective, final-answer accuracy provides an incomplete view of latent systems, and inspection of the thought representation should accompany it. Finally, decoded REST thoughts contain relatively more of the producers output than of its prompt, suggesting that property supervision can make latent communication easier to audit as agents increasingly communicate outside of text. Limitations. Due to the substantial computational cost, we do not sweep all combinations of properties and hyperparameters, as the number of required runs grows multiplicatively with each addition. Nevertheless, causality and minimality improve over CE at every weight we evaluate  (Table 11)  . cheap approximation to Stability is opted for due to compute limitations but still leads to performance gain. Another limitation is that REST trains only the outer link while the base LLMs and the inner link remain frozen, design choice to isolate the contribution of each property term. Extending REST to the training of the inner link or the agent is left to future work.

sections.title: B IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS
sections.content: B.1 BENCHMARKS MATH500 (Lightman et al., 2024) contains 500 test problems drawn uniformly at random from MATH, and its mix of subjects and difficulty levels is representative of the full test set. AIME2025 (Zhang & Math-AI Team, 2025) is the 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination, 30 problems whose answers are single integers. AIME2026 (Dekoninck et al., 2026) is the 2026 examination in the same format. GPQA-Diamond (Rein et al., 2024) is the most strictly filtered GPQA subset, 198 graduate-level multiplechoice questions in biology, chemistry and physics that both expert validators answered correctly and most non-experts missed. MedQA (Jin et al., 2021) draws multiple-choice questions from medical licensing examinations. LiveCodeBench-v6 (Jain et al., 2025) collects competition programming problems with release dates, which lets evaluation be restricted to window after models training cutoff. MBPP+ (Liu et al., 2023) re-evaluates the Python programming tasks of MBPP against many more test cases, and program counts as correct only when it passes every test. We report Pass@10 for AIME2025 and AIME2026, and Pass@1 for every other benchmark. The Code Gen. column reports MBPP+ on the Light system and LiveCodeBench-v6 on the Scaled system. Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems B.2 COMPARED BASELINES We compare REST against the following alternative auxiliary-loss baselines: CODI (Shen et al., 2025) trains continuous latent thoughts as the student in self-distillation setup, matching the students hidden states at one distillation token to those of teacher pass that reads the explicit chain of thought. We adapt its distillation loss as an auxiliary term on the outer-link cross-entropy objective, taking the consumers text transfer of Definition 2.1 as the teacher. SIM-CoT (Wei et al., 2026) supervises latent reasoning with an auxiliary decoder that reconstructs reasoningstep text from the implicit latents and is discarded at inference. We adapt its reconstruction loss as an auxiliary term on the outer-link cross-entropy objective, training per-stage decoder to reconstruct the producers output text from the transferred thought. B.3 HYPERPARAMETERS Optimization. We train the outer links for 20,000 steps at batch size 4 and maximum sequence length of 4096, in bfloat16. AdamW runs at learning rate of 5 104 under cosine schedule with 10 warmup steps, no weight decay, and gradients clipped at 1.0. Loss Terms. Every property term is swept over β {0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0}. For minimality, we set λ1 = 1.0 and λ2 = 0.3 and 0 for composition. For separability, we set = 64 at τ = 0.1. The CODI baseline is swept over {1, 10, 20} and SIM-CoT over {0.3, 1, 3}. Inference. thought spans at most 80 positions in training and fixed 32 latent steps at inference. We sample at temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95, lowered to 0.2 on MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench-v6. Table 5 provides max length for generated text.

Stepwise removal of thinking tokens moves an explicit chain of thought into the forward pass (Deng et al., 2025), dense embeddings stand in for compressed chain (Cheng & Van Durme, 2024), and latent and text tokens are mixed within one sequence (Su et al., 2025). Architectural variants add depth or recurrence at fixed points of the network, through dynamic depth scaling (Chen et al., 2025b) and through middle-layer recurrence across decoding steps (Cai et al., 2026). Recurrence can also carry persistent latent state across refinement steps, each supervised against ground-truth intermediate target (Li et al., 2026a). Huang et al. (2026b) prove that transformer internalizes chain of thought under staged curriculum, where the schedule for removing thinking tokens sets the number of training stages. Latent reasoning has also been applied to chemistry (Ye et al., 2026), built on hybrid state-space backbones (Wang & Reid, 2026), and cast as an exchange between fast and slow process (Coda-Forno et al., 2025). Supervising Latent Thoughts. Two objectives compress reasoning over decoded traces rather than over latent representations. Massoli et al. (2026) model reasoning trace under conditional information bottleneck, retaining only the information about the response that the prompt does not already supply, and optimize it as reinforcement learning objective with surprisal prior over traces. Conklin et al. (2026) treat training itself as lossy compression and report that pretrained models approach the information bottleneck bound, which links how much model compresses to downstream performance. Neither objective constrains thought transferred between agents. REST applies its terms at that transfer. Other work measures internal states without training on them, through uncertainty over the meanings model could generate (Kuhn et al., 2023) and through the geometry of reasoning trajectories in representation space (Zhou et al., 2026). Li et al. (2026b) intervene on individual latent steps and find that the steps carry different functions and route information non-locally. larger latent budget does not act as uniform extra depth. REST differs in the object it constrains and in the form of the constraint. Its terms apply to the latent thought at the point where one agent or one round passes it to the next, and each term is differentiable addition to the cross-entropy objective that leaves the architecture unchanged and adds no parameters at inference. 32 Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems
